newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on technicals, rangebound.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on technicals, rangebound.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on technical pressure with a lack of significant export business also cited, traders said.
Traders said the market remained under pressure from Friday's USDA October crop production report which showed potential U.S. 1996 U.S. corn production above expectations.
There also were ideas that the November USDA crop report may show an even greater number, the traders said.
Mid- and longer-term technical signals remained bearish, the traders said, with the key moving averages exerting downward influence.

But the nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December closed at 224.529 points, an indicator of a short term oversold market. Technical traders generally view an RSI of 30 or less as oversold territory while 20 or less is considered very oversold. Traders said there was support in the December near $2.80 per bushel and resistance at $2.90.
"There's support in the low 80s (Dec $2.80) in corn and beans ($6.80)," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Corn closed unchanged to 2-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with December unchanged at $2.83-1/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 37,000 contracts, down from 49,967 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 900 December $2.80 calls at 7-1/2 to 7-3/8 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 19,000 contracts, down from 22,173 Wednesday.
